input: Research noise ordinance rules before the block party

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Noise ordinances are hyper-local — city, county, or municipality determines which rules apply, so the location is the single most critical input.
The party date sets a hard deadline for when the research must be completed, which affects urgency and planning.
Ordinances vary by day of week and time window — knowing the planned hours of the party determines which specific rules are relevant.
Whether this person is organizing the party or just attending changes how actionable the research needs to be — an organizer may need to file permits, an attendee may just need general awareness.
Knowing where to look (city website, calling the non-emergency police line, HOA rules) depends on what resources and tools the person has already tried or has access to.
The output could range from a simple decibel limit and cutoff time to a full permit checklist — knowing what 'done' looks like shapes how deep the research needs to go.
The party may involve specific noise sources like a live band, DJ, or loudspeakers, which may be regulated differently from general crowd noise and should be specifically researched.

gold.taskTitle: Research noise ordinance rules for block party
gold.taskDescription: Look up the local noise ordinance regulations that apply to an upcoming block party event.

questions.title: What city or county is the block party in?
questions.description: Identify the specific municipality so the correct local ordinance can be located.

questions.title: What date is the block party happening?
questions.description: Pin down the event date to set a research deadline and determine weekday vs. weekend rules.

questions.title: What hours is the party expected to run?
questions.description: Establish the planned start and end times to identify which time-window noise rules apply.

questions.title: Are you organizing the party or just attending?
questions.description: Determine the user's role to calibrate whether the output needs to cover permits and compliance steps or just general awareness.

questions.title: Have you already checked any official sources for this?
questions.description: Find out what research has already been done to avoid duplication and identify the best next source to consult.

questions.title: What does a useful end result look like to you?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants a quick summary of key limits, a permit checklist, or something else entirely.

questions.title: Will there be amplified music or a PA system?
questions.description: Identify the specific noise sources planned so that any special amplification-related rules are included in the research.
